title: Density-first Console cards + table/ chart fallbacks for cross-browser polish
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: Several Console pages (dashboards, cost view, rollouts) have inconsistent density and breakpoints across browsers. On Safari and older Edge builds charts overflow, modal stacks create clipping with fixed-position elements, and table row wrapping causes a poor reading rhythm at small widths. Goal: Deliver a density-first responsive system that preserves readability, accessibility, and consistent behaviour across Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge. This ticket covers the design prototypes, interaction specs, and a set of cross-browser fallbacks for charts, tables, and modals so engineering can implement without regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Console card grid supports three density modes (compact, default, comfortable) with a single CSS variable switch and documented token map
Tables: column wrap rules and minimum column widths defined; horizontal scroll only appears after preserved reading order is violated; keyboard focus order remains row-first
Charts: SVG + Canvas progressive enhancement with a static-image fallback (PNG) for browsers that paint incorrectly; reduced-motion and high-contrast styles included
Modals: stacking rules prevent fixed header/footer clipping; modal stacking z-index map and focus-trap behaviours documented; mobile modal transforms degrade to full-screen correctly
Cross-browser QA checklist passes for Chrome (desktop & mobile), Firefox, Safari (macOS + iOS), Edge — no layout regressions at widths 320px–1920px
Design tokens, CSS examples, and Figma prototypes linked and approved by PM and Eng lead
Accessibility checks: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text, ARIA labels on chart controls, tab order verified in keyboard-only flows
